about: TBI's deck style: Simone's pages, positions and colours (her TBIComputer export of 2026-09-14), with CRC's panel counts stacked down each column (TBI redo ruling 5). Every rule here is true of her seeded deck and of the approved deck plan (work/tbi-redo/build-prep/deck-plan.csv); placement and label rules are what most of her sets follow, and the few of her own keys that do not are reported as warnings, never refused.
sources: docs/planning/2026-09-23-tbi-redo/STATE.md rulings 5, 24 and 29 (her pages, positions and colours; CRC panel counts stacked down each column; Avot may continue from column 6 into column 7; "Mourn Kadd 1", "Mourn Kadd 2")
work/tbi-redo/build-prep/deck-plan.csv and colour-map.json (every key: page, cell, label, colour, target, panel)

pages.purpose: JLicense, Visual T'filah and Donate slides in c1; the BirdDog camera pad in c2-c7
Friday evening in service order: Kabbalat Shabbat (2), Bar'chu to the Amidah (3), the Amidah (4), Aleinu to the close (5), songs and readings (6)
Occasional graphics (JLicense, Omer, national songs, Pride) and the OBS scene keys

columns.order: Her own order, as her deck had it: roughly the service from left to right, one prayer to a column. Not checked beyond the set rules.

fixed.keys: Companion's built-in page up, page number and page down in r0-r2 on every page (r3 may hold a graphic)

growth.rule: One key per panel, down the column; when the column is full below the last panel, the set continues at the top of the next column (Avot on page 3: r3c6 -> r0c7).

labels.rule: Her label for the prayer, then the panel number ("Mourn Kadd 1", "Mourn Kadd 2"; sometimes "pt 1").

colours.meaning: Her colour is the prayer's, not a role: every panel of a set on a page has one colour.

keyTypes: Graphics: one-step Toggle cue keys in her colours, with Requested and Rendered lights, anywhere outside c0 r0-r2.
BirdDog camera keys (page 1) and OBS scene keys (page 8), carried from her export unchanged.
Companion's built-in page up / number / down in c0 r0-r2 of every page; no Prev/Next chains, no switcher, no camera gesture.
